legend: Myxoid tumour is seen to abut the bronchial cartilage. The reticulated distribution of tumour cells is appreciable.
The lobulated architecture is striking, with cords and strands of spindle and stellate cells dispersed in the prominent myxoid stroma.

At high magnification, the cells are typically bland and are most frequently spindled to stellate, with relatively small vesicular nuclei and fibrillary cytoplasm. They are dispersed as cords and strands within the abundant, lightly basophilic myxoid stroma.
Spindle and rounded cells with typically bland nuclei show a lace-like or reticular architecture within sparsely cellular myxoid stroma, with a mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate.

FISH shows split red and green signals (thin arrows) with EWSR1 break-apart probes in tumour nuclei, consistent with the presence of rearrangements of this gene, contrasting with the fusion signal in a non-rearranged gene (thick arrow).

legend: Direct sequencing confirms the presence of EWSR1-CREB1 fusions, which predominantly involve exon 7 of each gene (lower diagram) or more rarely occur between exon 7 of EWSR1 and exon 8 of CREB1 (upper diagram).
